He reads it once. Reads it again. Behind him, Dani goes very still on the couch, a bowl of cereal halfway to her mouth, wearing his hoodie, the one with the burn hole on the cuff.

"I'm muted," she whispers.

"You're not," he whispers back, and four thousand people type the same thing at once.

Twenty minutes later, after an emergency "be right back" screen that fools no one, the friend server has opinions.
